label: Retail shop
tagline: Run the stock room of a corner shop
opening: It's your first morning as the stock assistant at **<<biz>>**. The owner wants a program that will one day run the whole stock room. Every program starts the same way: by saying something.
rule: The owner has a rule: when a product is down to **<<level>> or fewer**, it must be reordered. Right now nobody notices until a shelf is empty.
scene: A customer asks: "Do you have <<n2>>?" Staff shouldn't have to read the whole report. The system needs a quick lookup, and it must cope with things you don't stock.

action.name: restock
action.doc: add the delivery to the units on hand

glossary: A shop's unique code for one product, so two similar items never get mixed up.
How many units of a product are on the shelf right now.
The stock level at which you must order more.
Money tied up in a product: units times price.
Stock that disappears through theft, damage or errors. Reports help you spot it.
The paper that comes with a delivery, listing what was sent.
A count of everything on the shelves, compared with the records.
py_uses: Forecast which products will sell out before the weekend
Print shelf labels and price lists from a spreadsheet in seconds
Track daily sales and spot the slow movers
